newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TENS OF THOUSANDS WATCH CHELSEA BRING HOME CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TENS OF THOUSANDS WATCH CHELSEA BRING HOME CUP.

text.p: Tens of thousands of singing and chanting fans thronged the streets of south-west London on Sunday to watch Ruud Gullit's Chelsea bring the English F.A. Cup to Stamford Bridge for the first time in 27 years.

Police closed off streets and an underground station as fans, decked in blue, cheered the team's open-topped bus which made its way down the fashionable King's Road to the ground at the less prosperous end of the Fulham Road.
Houses and shops along the route were decorated with ribbons and posters. Small children flung shirts, scarves and T-shirts up to the players to sign and drop back into the heaving crowds.

Chelsea, who included only four Englishmen in a team of two Italians, a Romanian, a Norwegian, a Scot, one Welshman and a Frenchman, beat Middlesborough 2-0 on Saturday to lift the world-famous trophy -- symbol of English football.
Gullit, who has won the European championship as captain of the Netherlands as well as league and European trophies with AC Milan, became the first foreign manager to win the F.A. Cup.
Italian midfielder Roberto Di Matteo made history by scoring the fastest goal at the Wembley final, putting the ball past Middlesbrough 'keeper Ben Roberts in 43 seconds.
And Welsh international striker Mark Hughes picked up a record fourth winner's medal after three victories with his former club Manchester United.
Eddie Newton, who scored Chelsea's second goal, said the win had cancelled out the memory of losing the 1994 final 4-0 to Manchester United.
"There's no better feeling than scoring in the F.A. Cup," Newton said. "It's something special and makes up for being out for eight months with a broken leg and then a knee injury."
Chelsea, who won the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1971, go into that competition again next season.
Captain Dennis Wise said: "Last time we were in the Cup winners' Cup we got to the semifinal and with this team people might be a little bit worried about facing us."
The players were leaving London later on Sunday for a club trip to Malaysia.
